question: What is the central angle of a sector with an arc length of 10 cm in a circle of radius 5 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Central angle (θ) in radians = **Arc length (s) ÷ Radius (r)**

θ = 10 cm ÷ 5 cm = 2 radians

**∴ The correct answer is 2 radians.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Arc length** (s) = 10 cm

⇒ **Radius** (r) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ s = r × θ (where θ is the **central angle** in radians)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 10 = 5 × θ

⇒ θ = 10 ÷ 5

⇒ θ = 2 radians

**∴ The correct answer is 2 radians.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert an angle from radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π. 1 radian ≈ 57.3°.

Area of a Sector

The area (A) of a sector can be calculated using A = (1/2) × r² × θ or A = (1/2) × r × s.

Definition of 1 Radian

A radian is the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle.
